citation.sourceDocument: Ohio Rev. Code §5747.02(A)(3)(c) — for taxable years beginning in 2026 and thereafter, $332.00 plus 2.75% of the amount in excess of $26,050
citation.sourceNote: Ohio taxes NONBUSINESS income on a schedule that is identical for every filing status — Ohio does not widen its brackets for couples. HB 96, the FY2026-27 budget, finished the multi-year flattening by retiring the 3.125% band that applied above $100,000 in 2025, so from tax year 2026 there is one taxed band. The statute is quoted exactly: ORC 5747.02(A)(3) exempts the balance outright when it is 'equal to or less than twenty-six thousand fifty dollars', and §5747.02(A)(3)(c) reads 'For taxable years beginning in 2026 and thereafter, $332.00 plus 2.75% of the amount in excess of $26,050.' THE $332 IS A REAL CLIFF, not a rounding artifact: a filer at $26,050 owes nothing and a filer at $26,051 owes $332.03. It is the frozen residue of the graduated schedule Ohio used to run below the threshold (the 2024 figure was $360.69, the 2025 figure $342.00), and it is modeled through the engine's `baseTax` bracket field. Worked example, single $60,000 of Ohio taxable nonbusiness income: tax = $332.00 + 2.75%·(60,000 − 26,050) = $332.00 + $933.63 = $1,265.63. Ohio has no standard deduction; the engine's starting point is Ohio adjusted gross income. Two Ohio reductions are omitted at launch fidelity, both erring high. First, the §5747.025 PERSONAL EXEMPTION — $2,400 per person at Ohio AGI of $40,000 or less, $2,150 from $40,001 to $80,000, and $1,900 above $80,000 — which this engine cannot express because it varies with income rather than filing status; for a single filer at $60,000 it would cut about $59. Second, the Business Income Deduction, the joint-filing credit, the retirement-income credit, and Ohio's other credits. Business income is separately taxed at a flat 3%, which the wage engine does not reach. Ohio's ~600 MUNICIPAL income taxes are opt-in `localAddOns` here rather than automatic, so a city resident must select their city. Verified verbatim against Ohio Rev. Code §5747.02 on 2026-08-29; the Department of Taxation's Annual Tax Rates page still stops at tax year 2025.
